A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Ov3R and provide readable text, equations, six figures and six tables supporting comparison. All 10 pages of v1 and 11 pages of v2 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Tables 1–6 report original reconstruction, tracking, segmentation and ablation results on Replica, 7Scenes and ScanNetv2.

after.justification: Tables 1–6 retain original empirical evaluations, including revised Ov3R segmentation results in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The specified 2D–3D OVS procedure changes substantially. V1 extracts CLIP features from full, cropped and masked RGB images; v2 uses cropped and masked feature maps predicted by CLIP3R. Figure 4 and the fusion equations also change attention inputs and query/key/value roles. These differences revise one core module, although the overall two-module framework remains.

E1.justification: Both train reconstruction on ScanNet++, Aria Synthetic Environments and CO3D-v2, and segmentation on ScanNet++. Evaluation retains Replica, 7Scenes and ScanNetv2, including both ground-truth and CLIP3R geometry settings.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain the same comparators in corresponding experiments. Reconstruction baselines and the OpenScene, OpenNeRF, HOV-SG, Open3DIS, O2V-mapping and OVO comparisons are unchanged. The added SemanticFusion citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain eight Replica scenes, five ScanNetv2 scenes, one-in-twenty frame sampling on 7Scenes, the same class sets, geometry conditions, metrics and stated training budgets. No new evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Tables 5–6 retain identical ablations of CLIP insertion, CLIP supervision, DINO and the 3D encoder, including their values. Figures 5–6 retain the same reconstruction and semantic-query examples. No robustness or error analysis is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Results remain point estimates without statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 replace Ov3R segmentation scores. Under ground-truth geometry, Replica mIoU/mAcc changes from 30.7/41.3 to 31.9/42.3, ScanNet20 from 42.3/56.2 to 43.6/57.8, and ScanNet200 from 18.6/27.6 to 19.4/28.5. CLIP3R-geometry scores also increase. Baseline, reconstruction, tracking and ablation values remain unchanged; the replacement scores' origin is not explained.

T1.justification: Attention equations receive substantive mathematical corrections, including transposes and normalization by sqrt(d), replacing feature-valued denominators. Equations 4–5 explicitly use L1 norms where v1 described its L1 distance as Euclidean. These revise existing definitions; no theorem, proof or theoretical analysis is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: RGB-only open-vocabulary reconstruction, complementary CLIP3R and OVS modules, semantic–geometric alignment, modular operation and state-of-the-art reconstruction and segmentation.

C2.justification: The fusion rationale changes from raw CLIP's weak detail and object boundaries to explaining that CLIP3R features inherit limited 3D structural information from 2D supervision. Benchmark interpretations and the limitation concerning inaccurate recovered camera poses remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures retain the same hardware, 24 encoder and 12 decoder blocks, window lengths of 5 and 11, 15 OVS training epochs, batch size 512, and named feature encoders. Neither version adds code or data access instructions.

R1.justification: V2 adds the bibliographic citation for the already discussed SemanticFusion. It also changes the description of the same cited MoGe work from novel-view synthesis to single-image metric depth estimation. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the OVS explanation, now organized explicitly around scene, instance and masked feature streams. Terminology, subsection numbering and citation style also change, while the overall section order and most introductory and experimental prose remain.

P2.justification: Figures 3–4 become separate full-width architecture diagrams instead of small single-column diagrams; Figure 4 is substantially redrawn to show CLIP3R features, cropping and masking. The author block, headings, typography and page composition are reformatted throughout. Result figures and table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves methodological readability through explicit attention definitions, clearer feature-flow explanations and larger architecture diagrams. These are concrete gains, but empirical support is not broadened. Tables 3–4 change without explaining the replacement scores, while Table 6 retains earlier full-model values without clarifying their relationship to the revised results, limiting the overall improvement.
